standard.title: Analysing Patterns, Trends and Anomalies
standard.description: analyse and connect a variety of data and information to identify and explain patterns, trends, relationships and anomalies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify patterns and anomalies from representations (AC9S7I05, 7-8 band). They now extend to analysing data from multiple sources, connecting patterns across datasets, evaluating graph extrapolation validity, and identifying proportional relationships.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify and describe patterns, trends, proportional relationships and anomalies across multiple data sources, connect patterns across datasets, and evaluate the validity of extrapolating beyond observed data.

nodes.label: Patterns, trends, relationships and anomalies are identified across multiple sources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse data from multiple sources, identify patterns, trends and proportional relationships, recognise anomalies, and connect consistent patterns across different data sets.
nodes.minimum_width: Students identify a pattern or trend in data from at least two different sources and connect them, and identify at least one anomaly.
nodes.typical_width: Students analyse atmospheric CO₂ data from ice cores and monitoring stations to identify patterns and connect them; analyse heat transfer data to identify proportional relationships; examine radioactive decay data across tables, graphs and simulations; compare published with experimental sound insulation data and identify systematic trends in differences; recognise anomalies and distinguish them from expected variation.
wider: Analyse representations of atmospheric CO₂ from ice cores and monitoring stations — identifying patterns, trends and inconsistencies across source types
Analyse heat transfer data through insulating layers to identify the proportional relationship between thickness and heat transfer
Examine radioactive decay tables and graphs to identify the half-life pattern and predict mass changes over time
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to explain what patterns mean and evaluate extrapolation — moves that are impossible without first reliably identifying patterns and anomalies from multiple sources. Students who cannot identify cross-source patterns cannot interpret them or judge whether trends continue beyond observed data.

response_modes.reason: Students identify patterns within a single dataset but do not connect patterns across different source types (e.g. ice core data and monitoring station data showing the same CO₂ trend). Making the cross-source connection explicit — same pattern in independent sources strengthens the claim — is the scaffold for moving from observation to analysis.

success_criteria: Identifies a pattern or trend in data from at least two different sources and describes the connection between them
Identifies at least one anomaly in a data set and distinguishes it from expected variation

nodes.label: Patterns are explained and extrapolation validity is evaluated
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what identified patterns and anomalies indicate about the phenomenon being studied, and evaluate whether extrapolating beyond the observed data range is valid.
nodes.minimum_width: Students explain what one identified pattern indicates about the investigation question, and evaluate whether extrapolating from a given graph is valid.
nodes.typical_width: Students explain what identified patterns mean for the investigation question (not just describing the pattern, but interpreting it); explain what anomalies might indicate; evaluate when graph extrapolation is valid and when it overreaches the data; and discuss what additional data would be needed to support a claimed extrapolation.
wider: Discuss the validity of extrapolating from a graph — examining cases where extrapolation is reasonable and cases where it misleads

Compare published sound insulation data with experimentally determined values and explain the systematic pattern in differences — examining what the discrepancy indicates about experimental conditions vs standardised testing
Examine a case where an anomaly led to a significant scientific discovery — connecting pattern-and-anomaly analysis to how science progresses

response_modes.reason: Students readily describe what a pattern looks like without explaining what it means — they report 'as X increases, Y decreases' without connecting this to the scientific question. Similarly they extend graph lines beyond data without evaluating validity. The reasoning chain (what does this pattern tell us about the phenomenon? → is the relationship likely to continue outside the observed range? → what would need to be true for extrapolation to be valid?) is the scaffold that moves description to analysis.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The extrapolation validity question is a genuinely rich analytical direction that applies across all Y9 data contexts. The anomaly-to-discovery connection (AC9S9H01) provides a cross-strand enrichment that elevates pattern analysis from a technical skill to a scientific practice.
success_criteria: Explains what an identified pattern indicates about the phenomenon being studied — not just describes the pattern
Evaluates whether extrapolating from a given graph is valid and explains the reasoning
